claims.text: The Twelve-Factor App lists twelve factors; factor III, Config, says to store config (everything that varies between deploys) in the environment, strictly separated from code, and gives the test of whether the codebase could be made open source at any moment without compromising credentials.
Recreating donhang-api with a different JWT_SIGNING_KEY keeps the same image id (donhang-api:stage-1); docker inspect donhang-api --format {{.Image}} prints the same sha256 id before and after.
claims.source_hint: generator check on the running lab (sha256:e29a55ac5d91... before, during and after)

claims.text: git grep -n "Host=" in DonHang.Api, DonHang.Infrastructure and DonHang.Domain at stage-1 finds only DesignTimeDbContextFactory.cs, used only by dotnet ef at design time (per its comment) with password design-time-only.

appsettings.json holds only values that are the same everywhere; the connection string, signing key and ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT come from docker-compose.yml; the database password inside the connection string and the signing key come from the untracked .env.
This course adopts the factors one at a time as the app needs them; building once and running the same image everywhere depends on config being outside the image.
The image donhang-api:stage-1 contains no connection string or signing key used by the running API; the only address/password in it is the design-time string compiled into DonHang.Infrastructure.dll.
